item.text:
“S. 2817, the Superintelligence Prohibition Act” >>> [CHECK: the opening says the markup is Thursday, October 15, but the votes section later says Thursday, October 14.]

“the stakes for our coverage has never been higher” >>> “the stakes for our coverage have never been higher”

“federal goverment's” >>> “federal government's”

“more then ever” >>> “more than ever”

“three cosponsors on the committee, Senators Okafor and Lindqvist” >>> [CHECK: the memo says there are three cosponsors but names only two.]

“it's definitions” >>> “its definitions”

“central principal” >>> “central principle”

“Section 5 sets the bill's enforcment regime” >>> “Section 5 sets the bill's enforcement regime”

“directly effect every company” >>> “directly affect every company”

“Senator Whitfield (R-OK)” >>> [CHECK: the memo identifies Whitfield as R-OH earlier.]

“narrows the registry in Section 5” >>> [CHECK: the registry is described as a Section 4 requirement above.]

“keeps the $10 million daily civil penalty” >>> [CHECK: Section 5 above gives the civil penalty as up to $1 million per day.]

“Senator Grant, who's support” >>> “Senator Grant, whose support”

“the amendment's changes is modest” >>> “the amendment's changes are modest”

“Senator Gallager” >>> [CHECK: confirm the spelling; the memo may mean Senator Gallagher.]

“of the committees 28 members, 13 are yes or leaning yes, 10 are no or leaning no, and 6 are undecided” >>> [CHECK: the counts add up to 29, not 28.]

“The undecided senators are Chen, Ellis, Alvarez, Pike, and Barlow” >>> [CHECK: this lists five undecided senators, but the preceding count says six.]

“before the markup on Thursday, October 14” >>> [CHECK: the memo elsewhere gives the markup date as Thursday, October 15.]

“in a seperate interview” >>> “in a separate interview”

“the list of undecided senators, along with their staff contacts, are attached” >>> “the list of undecided senators, along with their staff contacts, is attached”

“Commerce Commitee markup” >>> “Commerce Committee markup”

“as soon as the week November 16” >>> “as soon as the week of November 16”

“hearing … occured” >>> “hearing … occurred”

“a close compliment to S. 2817” >>> “a close complement to S. 2817”

“the the offices” >>> “the offices”

“to there senators” >>> “to their senators”

“you should recieve” >>> “you should receive”

“Our six Hill reporters” / “Each of our five Hill reporters” >>> [CHECK: the memo gives inconsistent numbers of Hill reporters.]
